recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It preserves the FHIR-39033 decision to retain the filter resource discriminator while aligning the authoritative element definitions with the current SubscriptionTopic model.
issue_request: FHIR-39033 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked whether Subscription.filterBy.resourceType was redundant with the resource on the matching SubscriptionTopic filter, and the resolution retained the discriminator because multi-resource subscriptions can have filters that apply only to selected resources.
initial_application: Commit c7be29dba236b8d76eba270510768fc0095a3313 applied the issue by adding multi-resource topic guidance to the Subscriptions Framework page and related Subscription and SubscriptionTopic resource-page guidance.
additional_context: FHIR-41197 later renamed Subscription.filterBy.resourceType to Subscription.filterBy.resource and is already represented on the combined branch. FHIR-46492 later moved SubscriptionTopic canFilterBy under trigger, leaving the Subscription.filterBy element definitions with stale pre-FHIR-46492 SubscriptionTopic.canFilterBy cross-references.
reconciliation: Changed source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml so Subscription.filterBy.resource references SubscriptionTopic.trigger.canFilterBy.resource and Subscription.filterBy.filterParameter references SubscriptionTopic.trigger.canFilterBy.filterParameter.
source_changes: source/subscription/structuredefinition-Subscription.xml: updated Subscription.filterBy.resource and Subscription.filterBy.filterParameter definitions from SubscriptionTopic.canFilterBy paths to SubscriptionTopic.trigger.canFilterBy paths.
